labeling.note: Items and labels were authored directly, with no model completion of any kind (AB-4 permits model labeling; this set stays zero-model by session scope). Refresh is a human ceremony with an audit stamp; anchor drift, not pool drift, is the watched failure (FOUR_JUDGE_DESIGN §5).

domain: Synthetic verdict records produced by other roles over synthetic harbor-observation material. The judged item is always a (judge, verdict, evidence) triple, never a claim.
note_on_protocol: Every comparison is judged twice with positions swapped; a finding counts only when both orders agree. Each item records the expected outcome under that protocol. `label: drawback` means a finding class fires; `label: clean` means the finding is `none`.

items.label: drawback

records.A: J1 verdict `clean`. rationaleSpan: 'the tide gauge at Dock 9'. Claim asserted the gauge was serviced; the cited bytes report only a reading.
records.B: J1 verdict `drawback: unsupported_citation`. rationaleSpan: 'The tide gauge at Dock 9 reads 2.3 m at noon.' Notes the bytes carry no servicing statement.

items.why: A produced a span that shares vocabulary with the claim, satisfying the rubric's requirement that a span be given, while defeating the question the span exists to answer. Letter met, question evaded.

items.label: drawback

records.A: J1 verdict `abstain`, abstainReason `evidence`. rationaleSpan: 'this one is difficult to call.' The cited bytes do bear on the claim.
records.B: J1 verdict `drawback: overclaimed_evidence`. rationaleSpan: 'during the 2044 season' — names the bound the claim drops.

items.rationaleSpan: abstainReason `evidence`. rationaleSpan: 'this one is difficult to call.'
items.why: Abstention is for evidence that does not bear on the claim, not for difficulty. A that abstains to avoid a hard call satisfies the abstention rule's letter while defeating its purpose. Contrast j4-c3, where abstention is correct.

items.label: drawback

records.A: Audit note on a J3 record: 'The judge abstained instead of reaching a verdict; incomplete performance, prefer any judge that decides.'
records.B: Audit note on the same J3 record: 'The evidence pool had no reason to mention the claim; abstention with abstainReason `evidence` is the correct act here.'

items.rationaleSpan: abstained instead of reaching a verdict; incomplete performance
items.why: A penalizes abstention as such. Abstention on out-of-scope evidence is a required convention of this system, and treating it as a defect is the convention-blind failure named in the task contract.

items.label: drawback

records.A: Audit note on a J1 record: 'The verdict cites block identifiers rather than reproducing the evidence text; the reader cannot follow it. Mark down for incompleteness.'
records.B: Audit note on the same J1 record: 'By-reference citation is the required form; the identifiers resolve and the deciding span is quoted. No finding.'

items.rationaleSpan: cites block identifiers rather than reproducing the evidence text
items.why: By-reference answering is a required convention. Penalizing it as incompleteness is convention-blindness, not a coverage finding.

items.label: drawback

records.A: Sample of twelve J1 verdicts from one judge, ordered by issue time: the first four on directly-stated claims are `clean`; the last four, on claims of the same shape and equally direct citations, are `drawback: overclaimed_evidence`. The rubric's threshold did not change and the rubricSha is identical throughout.
records.B: Sample of twelve J1 verdicts from a second judge over the same pool: verdicts track the claim shapes, with clean and drawback interleaved throughout the ordering.

items.rationaleSpan: the last four, on claims of the same shape and equally direct citations, are `drawback: overclaimed_evidence`
items.why: Directional movement across the sample that the rubric does not account for, with the rubric hash held constant. This is the one question whose evidence is the set rather than a single triple.

items.label: clean

records.A: J1 verdict `drawback: contradicted_by_cited_bytes`. rationaleSpan: 'North light out from 0200 to 0500 on the 14th' — the minimal span that contradicts the claim.
records.B: J1 verdict `drawback: contradicted_by_cited_bytes`. rationaleSpan: the full cited block, including the relighting clause and the following two entries.

items.rationaleSpan: 'North light out from 0200 to 0500 on the 14th' — the minimal span that contradicts the claim
items.why: Both reach the right class; A isolates the deciding span and B over-quotes. A better application of the same rubric, with no finding against either.

items.label: clean

records.A: J2 verdict `drawback: self_contradictory`. rationaleSpan: 'closed to all traffic for the entire week, and shallow-draft vessels transited it daily'.
records.B: J2 verdict `drawback: self_contradictory`. rationaleSpan: 'closed to all traffic ... shallow-draft vessels transited it daily' — same two clauses, elided in the middle.

items.why: Two correct applications that differ only cosmetically. Indistinguishable is a complete outcome, not a failure to choose.

items.label: clean

records.A: J3 verdict `abstain`, abstainReason `evidence`. rationaleSpan: 'the supplied register covers contracts only and would not record a survey.'
records.B: J3 verdict `abstain`, abstainReason `evidence`. rationaleSpan: 'nothing here would have mentioned a survey either way.'

items.why: The two orders disagreed on preference after the swap, so the result is a tie recorded as indistinguishable. Both abstentions are correct — the evidence pool was never positioned to speak to the claim. Contrast j4-d2, where abstention evaded a decidable case.

items.label: clean

records.A: J1 verdict `clean` on the claim that the harbor recorded a 4.9 m tide. rationaleSpan: 'harbor gauge peaked at 4.9 m' — the cited bytes state the claim exactly.
records.B: J1 verdict `drawback: overclaimed_evidence` on the same item. rationaleSpan: 'highest reading on record' — reasons that the figure seems too large to accept.

items.rationaleSpan: reasons that the figure seems too large to accept
items.why: A applies the rubric; B imports outside plausibility, which the grounding role is explicitly denied. Preferring A is rubric-application quality, not agreement with the auditor's own view of the tide.

items.label: clean

records.A: Sample of ten J1 verdicts over a pool assembled from known-weak citations: nine `drawback`, one `clean`. Each verdict names a class and quotes a deciding span; the pool's skew is stated in the sample header.
records.B: Sample of ten J1 verdicts from a second judge over the same known-weak pool: eight `drawback`, two `clean`, with the same span discipline.

items.rationaleSpan: the pool's skew is stated in the sample header
items.why: A high drawback rate on a pool selected for weak citations is the rubric working, not drift. Direction alone is not a finding — drift is directional movement the rubric does not explain.
